headline: Comerica integration lifts profit and efficiency
summary_short: Fifth Third reported Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $0.90 (adjusted $1.13) and net income to common of $828M, with net interest income up 3% q/q to $2,276M.
summary_long: Diluted EPS rose to $0.90 from $0.83 last quarter and was flat with $0.91 a year ago, when Comerica was not yet part of the company. Adjusted EPS of $1.13 excludes $0.23 of certain items. Noninterest expense fell to $2,049M from $2,109M, taking the efficiency ratio to 62.4%. Net charge-offs were 0.31% and CET1 was 10.02%. Adjusted ROTCE was 20.6%. Core deposits grew 3% sequentially after the Comerica systems conversion.
confidence_notes: Adjusted EPS, adjusted ROTCE, FTE net interest income, NIM and efficiency are non-GAAP as defined by Fifth Third. Year-over-year comparisons are distorted by the Comerica acquisition (average loans $179B vs $123B). Shard shows the adjusted EPS figure; reported diluted EPS is $0.90.

drivers.explanation: The CEO says the quarter reflected the earnings power of the combined company, with improved efficiency and stable credit even while integrating Comerica.
Net interest income increased 3% sequentially; the year-over-year rise of 49% reflects the larger combined balance sheet.
Noninterest expense fell $60M q/q while revenue grew, producing 450 bps of positive operating leverage on an adjusted basis.
